channel.title: Hastings Daily: Council
channel.description: Local news for Hastings and St Leonards, three times a day.

item.title: Update: Hastings council seeks researchers to measure creative industries' economic impact
item.description: Hastings Council has confirmed it is seeking consultants to deliver a detailed assessment of the creative and cultural industries' economic impact, according to The Argus. Proposals for the study must be submitted by 5pm on Thursday, December 31.

item.title: Update: Hastings Cabinet to discuss fee freeze and heritage funding on 9 November
item.description: The Hastings Borough Council cabinet met on 9 November, and the decisions from that meeting are now recorded. The cabinet recommended the proposed 2027/28 fees and charges on existing services, to be implemented from 1 April 2027, to Full Council, and approved the Age Friendly Hastings strategy, action plan and evaluation framework. It also noted the successful securing of external funding totalling approximately £2.12 million for heritage, leisure and regeneration projects across Hastings.

item.title: Simpler disability allowance set for East Sussex care users
item.description: People in East Sussex who pay towards adult social care will get a simpler way to claim support for disability-related costs, the county council has approved.

item.title: Quit-smoking support brought to Conquest emergency department
item.description: Smokers in Conquest Hospital's emergency department can now get support to quit while they are in hospital.

item.title: Political accountability: County cabinet decisions on care payments and highway policy
item.description: The most significant items for the area this week were decisions published by the county council's lead cabinet members. At the Lead Member for Adult Social Care and Health meeting on Thursday 19 November at 2.00 pm, three decisions were published: the net to gross residential and nursing provider payments business case, the extension of the Integrated Health and Wellbeing Service contract, and proposed changes to Disability Related Expenditure. Area councillor Mark Estcourt was present. Councillor Johnny Denis (Green Party) declared a personal interest as the Lewes District Council cabinet member for community wellbeing, arts, culture, tourism and leisure, and did not consider it to be prejudicial.

item.title: Political accountability: Hastings Museum Committee meets, minutes not yet published
item.description: The Museum Committee met on Monday 16 November; no minutes are published yet, so no decisions are on the record. An officers' report to the committee said 37,510 people visited the museum in 2025/26 and recommended that the report be accepted and approval recommended to Cabinet.

item.title: Political accountability: Rother licensing panel considers Battle premises licence
item.description: The main local item this week came from the Licensing and General Purposes Committee's General Licensing Panel on Monday 16 November at 10.00 am, whose minutes have been published. The panel appointed Councillor Biggs as chair and considered the report on an application for a premises licence at Battle Abbey School Boarding House, Whatlington Road, Battle. The application covers regulated entertainment, late night refreshment and alcohol sales indoors and outdoors within the premises, Monday to Sunday, 12.00 to 00.30.

item.title: County council protects payments to Ukrainian family hosts
item.description: East Sussex County Council has stepped in to protect payments to families hosting Ukrainian refugees after the government said the 'thank you' payment would fall from £350 to £100 a month from January 2027.

item.title: County secures £2.9m in road maintenance funding after transparency report
item.description: East Sussex County Council has secured £2.9 million of incentive funding from the Department for Transport for road maintenance after publishing its Highway Maintenance Transparency Report.

item.title: Bexhill pedestrian safety improved with relocated Sea Road zebra crossing
item.description: A zebra crossing in Bexhill has been moved and widened after work to improve pedestrian safety on Sea Road was completed, the county council has confirmed.

item.title: Rother residents asked for views on waste and recycling collections
item.description: Residents across Rother are being asked for their views on the district's waste and recycling collections, Rother District Council has said.

item.title: Hastings water supply under pressure as reservoir stands at 41 per cent
item.description: Hastings households are being told the area's water supply is running well below normal levels, and that winter rain is now needed to top up reservoirs, rivers and groundwater.

item.title: Volunteers invited to care for Rother's micro woods during Tree Week
item.description: Residents are being invited to help look after three community micro woods across Rother during National Tree Week, which runs from 21 to 29 November.

item.title: Christmas parking concessions in Battle, Bexhill, Rye and Little Common
item.description: Rother District Council has published its Christmas parking concessions, with charges suspended in a selection of off-street car parks across Battle, Bexhill, Little Common and Rye from late November through December.

item.title: Planning roundup: new houses, surgery flats and games area among latest applications
item.description: Proposals for four new houses, the conversion of a former GP surgery into flats and a new outdoor sports facility are among the latest planning applications submitted to Hastings Borough Council, the Hastings Observer reports.

item.title: Refugee resettlement project reports 264 moved into work or education
item.description: Hastings Borough Council's Resettlement Employability Project has supported more than 384 people since launching in 2023, with 264 participants moving into employment or education, the council said. That includes 56 people so far this year.

item.title: Hastings council seeks researchers to measure creative industries' economic impact
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has issued a call out to consultants and research teams to undertake a study of what the creative and cultural industries bring to the town's economy.

item.title: Green Automotive Centre of Excellence opens at Ore Valley campus
item.description: A new Green Automotive Centre of Excellence has opened at East Sussex College Group's Ore Valley campus in Hastings.

item.title: Bexhill councillor raises pedestrian safety concerns over 146 homes plan
item.description: A Bexhill councillor has raised concerns over pedestrian safety as part of proposals to build 146 new homes on land off Spindlewood Drive in Little Common.

item.title: Hastings Museum opens sustainability exhibition with Natural History Museum and local students
item.description: Hastings Museum & Art Gallery is opening a new sustainability exhibition in partnership with the Natural History Museum and local students.

item.title: Hastings council approves £4.4 million for playgrounds, padel courts and heritage repairs
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has approved more than £4.4 million for projects across the town, covering playgrounds, sports facilities and improving some of the town's best-known historic attractions, The Argus reported.

item.title: Hastings asking rents up to 23% above ONS average, housing data shows
item.description: Median asking rents in Hastings are running well above the official average, with the gap on three-bedroom homes reaching 23%, housing website Dwellio says.

item.title: Hastings dog owners face £100 fine under updated dog control order
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has warned dog owners that fines are in force under an updated dog control order.

item.title: Claremont School submits plans for games area at Clyde House
item.description: A St Leonards boarding school has put forward plans to build an outdoor sports facility on a property it owns.

item.title: Update: Bexhill GP surgery closed today over 'unforeseen circumstances'
item.description: Sidley Medical Practice in Bexhill has reopened after Monday's closure. The practice said the situation affecting it has now been resolved and thanked patients for their patience. NHS Surrey and Sussex ICB said the surgery was temporarily closed after an issue with access to the building meant the team running the service could not enter; the matter was resolved with support from the police and access has now been restored. Patients were asked to consider contacting the practice later in the week for non-urgent enquiries, as phone lines may be busy.

item.title: Hastings council to freeze most parking charges in 2027/28
item.description: Hastings council has confirmed plans to freeze most pay-and-display parking charges for 2027/28, following three years of increases. Cabinet members backed the proposals on Monday (9 November) ahead of a full council vote.

item.title: Planning round-up: HMO proposals in St Leonards among latest applications
item.description: A series of planning applications have been submitted to Hastings Borough Council, including proposals for three houses in multiple occupation in St Leonards, according to a round-up of applications published by the Hastings Observer.

item.title: Bexhill GP surgery closed today over 'unforeseen circumstances'
item.description: Sidley Medical Practice, the Bexhill GP surgery on Turkey Road and Albert Road, is closed today. The practice said on its website that "due to some unforeseen circumstances we are unable to operate from our building today".

item.title: East Sussex joins national programme to use creative activities for health
item.description: East Sussex County Council has been selected to join a national programme that uses creative and cultural activities to improve health and wellbeing.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: The council's budget consultation has now opened and runs until 5pm on 16 December. People can take part via an online survey, by email to consultations@rother.gov.uk, or by post to the council's Town Hall in Bexhill. The council said it wants to understand the effect of the proposals before making final budget decisions.

item.title: Bexhill community hub to get more than £500,000 in developer funding
item.description: More than £500,000 has been allocated to create a new community hub in Bexhill town centre, Rother District Council said.

item.title: Health watchdog orders rapid improvements at Conquest Hospital emergency care
item.description: The Care Quality Commission has downgraded the urgent and emergency care service at the Conquest Hospital in St Leonards from 'good' to 'requires improvement' and ordered East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust to submit an action plan showing what action it is taking to make immediate improvements. The hospital's overall rating has moved from 'outstanding' to 'good'.

item.title: Rother council to invest £1.3m in seven local projects
item.description: Rother District Council has approved £1.3m from its Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) fund to support seven projects across the district, aimed at improving local facilities, enhancing accessibility and promoting sustainability.

item.title: Hastings council rejects community asset bid for St Leonards convent site
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has turned down a bid to list the former Convent of the Holy Child Jesus on Magdalen Road, St Leonards, as an Asset of Community Value.

item.title: New wheelchair and mobility scooter support group launched in Hastings
item.description: A new support group for residents who use wheelchairs or mobility scooters is being launched in Hastings.

item.title: Saxon Mount School submits plans to replace mobile classrooms with two-storey building
item.description: Saxon Mount School, in Edinburgh Road, St Leonards, has submitted a planning application to replace its four single-storey mobile classrooms with a new two-storey building.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Hastings council budgets £1,937,861 for St Mary in the Castle in 2026/27
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has budgeted spending of £1,937,861 on the Grade II* listed seafront building St Mary in the Castle in the 2026/27 financial year, with the majority set to come forward as capital spending.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Residents to have say on East Sussex supported housing strategy
item.description: People in supported housing across the district can have their say on how it should improve, Rother District Council has said.

item.title: Plans for 42 new homes by St Leonards' Bannatyne's Spa Hotel
item.description: Outline permission has been submitted to build up to 42 homes on land at Bannatyne's Spa Hotel in Hastings Road, St Leonards, according to the latest Hastings Borough Council planning applications.

item.title: Cabinet to consider £1.5m playground funding on Monday
item.description: More than £1.5m to improve playgrounds across the town is set to be considered at the council's Cabinet meeting on Monday evening.

item.title: Call for interest in future use of Sandhurst Recreation Ground
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is asking sports clubs, groups and organisations to register their interest in the future of Sandhurst Recreation Ground. The council wants to know how much demand there is for the sports pitches, which organisations would like to use the site, and whether it could be managed or developed by the community.

item.title: Have your say on renewal of five gated paths in Hastings and St Leonards
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is asking for views on plans to renew gating orders for five public rights of way in Hastings and St Leonards.

item.title: Update: White Rock Gardens could get covered padel and tennis courts
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has announced it is in line to receive £1.3million of investment funding to construct a new covered tennis and padel centre, with a projected overall cost of £1.8million and the council pledging £500,000 match funding.

item.title: West Hill Lift closed for urgent surveys and repairs
item.description: The West Hill Lift has been closed for essential surveys and repairs, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

item.title: Hastings Draft Local Plan: Convent site open for comment until 12 November
item.description: The deadline for the public to comment on the Hastings Borough Council's Draft Local Plan is Thursday 12 November, and one of the most argued-over parts of it is what happens to the Convent of the Holy Child Jesus in Lower Bohemia.

item.title: Council to seek group to take lease of Hollington Community Centre
item.description: East Sussex County Council is looking for a local group to take on the lease of Hollington Community Centre in Old Church Road, after saying the building needs significant investment to bring it back into good repair.

item.title: Update: Hastings Castle to get £288,500 from Historic England for repairs
item.description: Following the £288,500 Historic England award and a £200,000 contribution from the council, the first phase of conservation works at Hastings Castle has begun, with specialist contractors removing vegetation from sections of the castle walls and the motte. The works are due to be completed by 16 November.

item.title: Hastings council to consider Age Friendly strategy for older residents
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has drawn up an Age Friendly Hastings Strategy and Action Plan, with proposals to make the town more accessible and inclusive for people aged 50 and over.
